About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!

You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.

Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.

Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.

What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.

Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.

In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.

Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.

title: Trucking Dispatcher
description:
Zelh is seeking an experienced Trucking Dispatcher to support its growing fleet and help keep trucks loaded, moving, and profitable across the United States. The ideal candidate will have at least one year of hands-on experience dispatching trucks in the U.S. transportation market and will be comfortable managing the complete day-to-day movement of assigned trucks. This includes communicating directly with drivers, coordinating pickups and deliveries, resolving operational issues, and actively searching for loads to minimize empty miles and maximize truck utilization.
This is a proactive position. We are looking for someone who understands that successful dispatching is not simply monitoring trucks-the goal is to consistently find quality freight and keep drivers moving.
Key Responsibilities

• Manage and dispatch assigned trucks across East Coast, West Coast, and nationwide lanes.

• Maintain consistent communication with drivers regarding load assignments, pickup and delivery times, routes, delays, and operational issues.

• Actively search load boards and other available sources for freight that fits each truck's location, equipment, schedule, and desired lanes.

• Negotiate rates with freight brokers and work to secure profitable loads.

• Minimize deadhead and empty miles by planning ahead and identifying the next load before the current load is completed whenever possible.

• Coordinate pickups and deliveries and ensure drivers have all necessary load information and documentation.

• Track trucks and shipments throughout transit and proactively communicate delays or service issues.

• Build and maintain relationships with brokers and other transportation partners.

• Understand regional freight markets and recognize strong and weak lanes.

• Assist drivers with issues that arise while under load and work quickly to find solutions.

• Maintain accurate load, driver, rate, and operational information.

• Work closely with Brothers Freight leadership to maximize fleet utilization, service levels, and profitability.

Working conditions:

• Work schedule: Monday - Friday 8 am- 5 pm EST

• Competitive Salary in USD

• Remote mode of work

• 10+ business days of paid time off

• Team building and corporate events

• Equipment provided

• A supportive team

Requirements
Required Qualifications

• Minimum of 1 year of experience as a dispatcher within the U.S. trucking industry.

• Experience actively finding and booking loads, not solely tracking existing shipments.

• Strong understanding of U.S. geography, freight lanes, and trucking operations.

• Experience using load boards such as DAT, Truckstop, or similar platforms.

• Ability to communicate professionally and confidently with drivers and freight brokers.

• Experience negotiating freight rates is strongly preferred.

• Ability to manage multiple trucks and priorities simultaneously.

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to react quickly when loads, appointments, or driver schedules change.

• Strong written and verbal English communication skills.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of assigned trucks.

What Success Looks Like
A successful Brothers Freight dispatcher takes ownership of their assigned trucks from beginning to end. They know where their drivers are, what load they are currently running, when they will become available, and ideally what load they are running next. The objective is simple: keep the trucks loaded, minimize empty miles, communicate with the drivers, provide excellent service, and keep the operation moving profitably.
